components.name: Primary Button
components.description: One decisive local or public action.
components.css: .ds-primary { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--proof-on-fill); background: var(--proof); font: 600 16px var(--font-body); transition: 140ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-primary:hover { background: var(--proof-hover); } .ds-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-secondary { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--ink-strong); background: var(--paper-raised); font: 600 16px var(--font-body); transition: 140ms var(--ease-out); } .ds-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--proof); } .ds-secondary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Verified Status Chip
components.description: Text and color confirmation for a completed proof.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--proof); border-radius: var(--radius-pill); color: var(--proof-ink); background: var(--proof-soft); font: 500 11px var(--font-mono); }

components.name: Evidence Fingerprint
components.description: A complete technical value with a single proof accent.
components.css: .ds-evidence { padding: 20px; border-left: 3px solid var(--proof); color: var(--ink-strong); background: var(--paper-subtle); font-family: var(--font-body); } .ds-evidence span { display: block; margin-bottom: 8px; color: var(--proof); font: 500 11px var(--font-mono); letter-spacing: .07em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-evidence code { overflow-wrap: anywhere; font-family: var(--font-mono); }

components.name: Run Stage
components.description: One real pipeline stage with explicit result detail.

components.css: .ds-stage { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 28px 1fr; gap: 12px; color: var(--ink); font-family: var(--font-body); } .ds-stage > span { display: grid; width: 28px; height: 28px; place-items: center; border-radius: 50%; color: var(--white); background: var(--proof); font: 500 11px var(--font-mono); } .ds-stage strong { color: var(--ink-strong); font-size: 14px; } .ds-stage p { margin: 4px 0 0; color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.4; }

narrative.overview: FaceProof feels like a careful review desk built for a judge who has only a few minutes. Large editorial type establishes the claim, while thin rules, quiet paper tones, and a persistent run record expose the supporting work. The system rejects crypto spectacle and artificial certainty.
keyCharacteristics: Mineral paper instead of pure white or dark dashboard chrome.
One teal proof signal used for active, matched, and verified states.
Editorial display type paired with neutral body copy and mono evidence labels.
Real stage detail instead of decorative progress.
Thin rules and tonal surfaces instead of stacked card decoration.

rules.name: The One Proof Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal means that work is active, selected, matched, or verified. It is not a general decorative accent.

rules.name: The Public Write Rule
rules.body: The irreversible blockchain approval uses rust until confirmation. It must not look identical to an ordinary local action.

rules.name: The Claim and Evidence Rule
rules.body: Display type makes the claim once. Everything after it uses restrained title, body, and mono roles so evidence stays primary.

rules.name: The Desk Surface Rule
rules.body: Evidence panels sit on the page like organized documents. Do not make every section float.

dos: Do keep the source, score, threshold, and evidence fingerprint close to the selected result.
Do preserve useful partial results when a later stage fails.
Do use the exact six stage titles in the workbench and recording.
donts: Don't make the product resemble a cryptocurrency trading screen.
Don't use a neon cyber security dashboard.
Don't create a generic grid of statistic cards.
Don't turn a similarity score into a confidence percentage or identity claim.
